prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve. Asset type: production 2D Soldier survivor animation for Grave Accord. Image 1 is the approved complete idle strip for this exact facing; it locks identity, camera and equipment grip. Image 2 is the original shipped single-facing seed. Both references show the required direction; do not invent an opposite-facing view. Preserve the same young adult woman Mara Rook, chin-length wavy chestnut hair, dark navy peaked officer cap with a small brass badge/band, ragged long split navy-blue officer coat with restrained brass trim and a sleeve crest, charcoal trousers, brown leather lace-up boots and gloves, utility belt pouches, small brass belt chain and one cross-body strap matching the reference. ONE compact dark brass pistol stays in the physical RIGHT trigger hand with the LEFT hand supporting the grip. Keep the same compact pistol, two arms, face and cap in every pose; no rifle, second pistol, sword, holster swap, new hat, mirrored strap or added ornament. Use restrained dry black ink and matte opaque gouache, broad quiet color planes and selective practical contours. Avoid glossy gradients, excessive tiny scratches, decorative filigree or noise. Maintain two arms, two legs and one intact body/weapon in every pose.
Every pose faces SOUTH, toward the viewer in the exact original front/three-quarter game angle. Chest, head and boots stay toward the viewer; do not turn into an east/west side profile. Right rear-trigger hand stays on viewer LEFT; left forward-support hand on viewer RIGHT. Retain the original diagonal ready-gun angle.
Draw EXACTLY 4 full-body poses as one coherent attack sheet, arranged in one horizontal row of 4 complete poses on a wide transparent canvas. No additional figure. Action: One restrained stationary primary shot cycle: 1 upright aimed-ready stance matching the reference, 2 brace the SAME firearm with both original grips, 3 a small controlled recoil into the shoulders, 4 settle back toward pose 1. Keep boots planted, torso facing fixed and gun barrel rigid. No broad swing, spin, grip exchange, muzzle flash, projectile, casing, smoke, spark or painted effect. The game renders effects separately.
Every pose is one complete independent drawn body at ONE common character scale calibrated from upright pose 1. Crouched and resting poses retain their naturally lower height. Use roomy clear gutters between all cells and generous padding around the ENTIRE body/weapon/cape, with a consistent ground baseline in each row. Genuine RGBA transparency: alpha zero outside each figure and between limbs/props. No floor, shadow, backdrop, haze, vignette, glow, particles, checker pattern, text, labels, frame numbers or grid lines. Keep a coherent animation rather than unrelated character illustrations.
